storyTitle: From pixel to source in one interaction.
storyNote: The page and the source are two views of the same thing.
title: Visual workspace for Astro — Avocado
description: See your actual Astro site, navigate source-backed elements, inspect component props, compare responsive previews, and edit source in one local workspace.
headline: See the site Astro actually renders.
intro: Avocado runs your project's own development server and brings the rendered page into a source-aware visual workspace. The canvas is an interface to your existing project.

sections.title: The page and the source are two views of the same thing.

items.title: Canvas → Navigator
items.body: Click the thing you see. Find the source-backed node.

items.title: Navigator → Canvas
items.body: Choose an element in the hierarchy. See where it lives on the page.

items.title: Canvas → Inspector
items.body: Inspect the source file, tag, attributes, component props, and source location.

items.title: Canvas → Code
items.body: Go from rendered element to source without manually searching the repository.

sections.title: Inspect components without pretending components are boxes.
body: Avocado understands component boundaries in Astro projects. Enter a component. Inspect its declared props. Edit supported literal values. Move back out to the page.
When something requires code, open the source instead of forcing it through a visual abstraction.

sections.title: Responsive work without opening three browser windows.
body: Preview the page at desktop, tablet, and phone widths, or compare multiple sizes at once.
Zoom and pan the stage while keeping the project around it. When the embedded canvas is not enough, open the same page in your browser.

sections.eyebrow: Source is part of the product
sections.title: The code editor is not an escape hatch.
body: Some jobs are faster visually. Some jobs are easier in source. Avocado does not need one interface to win every time.
Open the code pane. Jump to the relevant source. Edit. Save. Return to the page. Keep moving.

sections.title: Understand CSS before changing it.
body: The Style view helps explain where a selected element's source-side styling comes from: property, value, selector, file, line, and origin. Use it to follow the cascade back into the project.
Current limitation: visual CSS editing controls and live computed-style editing are not yet part of the shipped Style surface.

sections.title: Variables turn CSS tokens into a project interface.
body: Instead of scanning stylesheets for every custom property, Avocado can organize project variables into a dedicated surface.
Stylesheet tabs. Groups. Modes. Comparable values. Reordering. Responsive typography checks. All while writing back to the CSS that already exists.

stages.title: Rendered button
stages.body: Start with the element on the page. This is an explanatory example of the source-selection workflow.

stages.title: Source selection
stages.body: Connect the rendered element to its component.

stages.title: Component
stages.body: Follow the selection into the component's source file.

stages.title: Source
stages.body: Read the relevant implementation and continue in code when that is the clearer interface.

finalTitle: Don't rebuild the website inside your website builder.
finalBody: Build on the website you already have.
